explanations: handleBatch applies every event in the partition batch concurrently with Promise.all. Events for the same order (same key, same partition) arrive in order, but their apply calls interleave: both can read the same existing view before either writes, both pass the version check, and the put that finishes last wins. An older status such as 'preparing' can overwrite 'ready', and customers can be notified out of order. The version check only works if reads and writes for one order are serialized; events should be applied sequentially (or grouped by orderId and run sequentially per group).

apply returns false when event.version <= existing.version, so no put and no notification occur. handleBatch records an 'order_status.skipped' metric and commits the last offset. Nothing throws, and there is no buffering.

decode catches the JSON error, increments 'order_status.unparseable' and returns null; the filter drops it. The commit uses the last message in the batch, so the bad message's offset is committed too. There is no DLQ or re-parse.

apply checks TERMINAL.has(existing.status) before the version check and returns false, so neither put nor notify runs. The version comparison is never reached, and the notifier only ever targets the customer.
